public_rationale: The funding records challenge the claim that investment appetite had disappeared. They do not settle the broader prediction of eventual collapse: Zitron supplied no deadline and explicitly allowed further raises to prolong the boom. Treating a successful round as a conclusive refutation would discard that qualification.
limitations: An assessment confined to the present-tense funding-appetite clause could differ from this assessment of the complete forecast.
Company financing announcements do not establish profitability or technical progress.

our_interpretation: The main forecast is an eventual collapse of the generative AI investment boom through inadequate funding.
The ordinary reading of market appetite is willingness to finance further development. No numerical threshold is supplied.

The surrounding passage explicitly allows further fundraising to prolong the boom. A subsequent successful round therefore challenges the description of current appetite without conclusively disproving eventual collapse.
‘It seems’ expresses uncertainty; it is not an antecedent that must occur.
This is a sector-wide forecast, rather than a claim about a particular company's financial metric.
criteria.support_condition: A decisive sector-wide breakdown in financing causes the generative AI investment boom to collapse. Isolated business failures or a temporary investment slowdown are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event rules out the predicted funding-driven collapse under the stated scope. Continued funding for a finite period challenges the near-term description but cannot rule out an undated eventual collapse.
